title: Is anyone working on a shared project? Most projects I see are solo developed, myself included
author: jaykrown
selftext:
One shotted this tiny farm game with Sonnet 5.5 High just as a test to see if I could get the gameplay loop working in one go, and it worked.

I think if I take on any new projects they will be through a shared git repository. I see so many people working on their own things. Anyone have any projects they're working on with others through a shared git or something?

comments.author: United-Tour5043
comments.body: i think its because we dont have online 3rd places anymore, i think we need to bring back forums and clans, who are with me?

replies.author: GlobalCurry
replies.body: Yeah I remember back in the day I could get a group together from various forums to build fan games and stuff and we'd have yahoo or msn or skype groups and message boards.

replies.author: Novaworld7
replies.body: why do you need a forum to work with anyone? Why not just use discord?

comments.author: Danoweb
comments.body:
My business partner and I are working together.

I handle the technical side of things, he is great with art.  We are both using AI just in different ways

comments.author: Shrineheart
comments.body:
Not really. Most of the people I know have day jobs like I do and don't have an active interest in game dev. I do have some good friends in tapping in for narrative help because I want to be sure I handle certain topics they're versed in well though. One has offered to learn Godot to pitch in too.
My AI is my dev partner. My fiance looks over ui decisions because he does ui design.

comments.author: Significant-Neck-520
comments.body:
I've made a git of the graphics stuff I'm working on, and looking for projects that share their assets. They are not ready yet, tough, so they might be hard to work with -  actually, I havent tested how to produce the blender file from the code, but claude said it is possible.
https://github.com/danielgruginski/MedievalVillageKit

comments.author: Shuma665
comments.body: moving at the speed most vibers are going would likely be extremely problematic withouf extreamly good code promotion and release managment flows.  Teams greater than 2 would likely screw them selves over 3 times a day with a 5-99k PR

replies.author: geddy
replies.body: Yeah we have to be super careful at work and end up splitting branches like crazy so the (human reviewed) PRs don’t explode. Luckily the models are really great at maintaining branch chains and rebasing them when changes hit the main branch so that’s never been a big issue. Just gotta be respectful with the PR size and split branches by sub-feature touched.

comments.author: Manifesto-Engine
comments.body: I could use the help with Asterra. :) plus it would be fun to collab.

comments.author: geddy
comments.body: I thought about this. It would definitely require working on different parts of the agents would clash with merge conflicts. Then again the agents could solve merge conflicts fairly easily lol so I suppose it would work fine, so long as you use a versioning system and aren’t just remotely hitting a server and letting your agent go nuts.

replies.author: AriaTorres2
replies.body: I’d still add a quick shared playtest after merging. Two branches can merge cleanly while disagreeing about the game state, like one changing crop IDs and another using the old IDs in the save system. For a farm game, a small check could be: plant → save → reload → harvest. Agreeing on the save format and who owns shared systems before splitting up the work would help too.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body: I never had any success finding people to work with even when I joined gamejams. its fine. that's what AI is for I suppose

replies.author: RRetr0_
replies.body: Well people usually join Gamejams in made groups in order for them to win instead of finding other members (its a relatively low chance you will find teams looking for members) But you can find people across platform forums, discord, other groups online who are willing to participate with you.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: its fine. gamejams are usually anti-ai so I pretty much gave up that part of gamedev when I hopped over to this side

comments.author: RRetr0_
comments.body:
A) Would love to collab if anyone is down,   
B) Yes there used to be forums and groups across multiple platforms but they have died down and dont exist as of now, But there is one silver lining -   
C) The best “merged” gaming or game devving related community would be GDL on discord, its an official discord Partnered Server with 140,000 members and there is a dedicated channel for AI Devving; Link to said server would be: [https://discord.com/invite/gamedev](https://discord.com/invite/gamedev)

replies.author: RRetr0_
replies.body: And yes i did have a project in the past which did have shared members and my programmers were working on a shared git file (2 programmers) but due to some age-related, and other internal issues the project was disbanded around 1 year and 7 months ago
